spec.title: Write a lang package
spec.p: A lang package teaches an agent how to write in a language or a notation: the idioms, the constraints, the shape of a good file. This page writes one and explains how vibe recognises it as a language discipline.
spec.prompt: Create a lang package org.acme/sql-style in packages/sql-style of the current VibeVM project: a guide on how our team writes SQL, with a boot snippet that names the three rules an agent must always follow and a guide document with the full idioms, examples and the reasons behind them. Run vibe check on it. the vibevm skill installed for your agent; a project with `vibe.toml` at the root `packages/sql-style/vibe.toml` declares `kind = "lang"` with a boot snippet; the guide under `vibevm/vibespecs/` has anchored sections the snippet cites; `vibe check` reports no errors vibe check --path packages/sql-style --quiet grep -q "kind = \"lang\"" packages/sql-style/vibe.toml

what-happens.title: What happens
what-happens.p: The agent creates the package skeleton, writes the guide and its snippet the way a flow's are written, and sets the kind to `lang`. The difference from a flow is the genre, not the mechanics: a flow says how the team works, a lang package says how to write in something, and the kind tells an agent, a registry and the site which is which before the file is opened.

what-a-lang-is.title: What a lang package is, and is not
what-a-lang-is.p: The genre is wider than programming languages: a guide to a query language, a configuration notation, a documentation dialect or a house style of a language all fit. What does not fit is a bundle of tools; that is a stack. The examples in the public registry are the AI-Native language guides for Rust, TypeScript and Go, each shipping a guide, a set of cards and a runnable toolchain.

An AI-Native language is recognised by one thing only: its dependency on the shared discipline core, `org.vibevm.ai-native/core-ai-native`. Not by its group, not by its name. A third party may publish its own language discipline in its own group and be recognised the same way, so the discipline is not a closed club.

families.title: When a language brings tools
families.p: A language guide that also ships tools, a checker, a formatter, a type oracle, becomes a family: the guide package `<family>-lang`, a server package `<family>-mcp` that serves the same tools to agents, and a bundle `<family>` that pins both at one version. The members move in unison; a consumer requires the bundle and gets a tested set.
The family stem leads every named surface: crates, binaries, skills and the server all carry the `<family>` prefix, so everything of one language sorts and reads together.

by-hand.title: By hand
by-hand.p: 1. Create the package and set the kind:
2. Write `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/sql-style.xml` with the rules an agent must follow every time, and the guide under `vibevm/vibespecs/lang/sql-style/` with the reasons, the idioms and the examples.
3. Declare `[boot_snippet] source = "vibevm/vibespecs/boot/sql-style.xml"`, `category = "stack"`, so that the language rules come after the team's flows in a consumer's reading list.

edge-cases.title: Edge cases and rules
edge-cases.p: What a language brought that can be run is answered by `vibe tools`, not by the kind: the boot lane says which disciplines are installed, the tools registry says what they brought.
Before the `lang` kind existed, language guides were stacks; a `stack` package that is really a guide should move to `lang` at its next version, so that the word means one thing.
